en: Mám rád, páči sa mi, chutí mi
t: Mám rád, páči sa mi, chutí mi

a2-u3-pozvanka.na-vianoce.note.en: It's **advent**, the weeks before Christmas, and Emma isn't going home to Ireland this year. **Vianoce** is always plural: Vianoce sú v decembri.
a2-u3-pozvanka.na-vianoce.note.t: Hozir **advent** — Rojdestvodan oldingi haftalar. Emma bu yil uyiga, Irlandiyaga bormaydi. **Vianoce** doim koʻplikda keladi: Vianoce sú v decembri. = Rojdestvo dekabrda.

a2-u3-pozvanka.chces-prist-k-nam.en.en: Do you want to come to us for Christmas?

a2-u3-pozvanka.chces-prist-k-nam.note.en: **k nám** = to our place. Lucia is inviting Emma home to her family in Žilina.
a2-u3-pozvanka.chces-prist-k-nam.note.t: **k nám** = biznikiga, bizning uyimizga. Lusiya Emmani Jilinaga, oʻz oilasinikiga taklif qilyapti.

en: Do you want to go home for Christmas?
Do you want to come to us for Christmas?
Do you want to come to the Christmas party?

a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-chces-prist-k-nam..en: **k nám** means to our place: prísť k nám = to come to us. Going home would be ísť **domov**.
a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-chces-prist-k-nam..t: **k nám** — biznikiga: prísť k nám = biznikiga kelmoq. Uyga borish esa ísť **domov** boʻlardi.

a2-u3-pozvanka.rada-pridem.en.en: I'd love to come! (a woman speaking)

a2-u3-pozvanka.rada-pridem.note.en: **rád, rada** + a verb = glad to, happy to. Prídem points to the future, like kúpim: I'll come.
a2-u3-pozvanka.rada-pridem.note.t: **rád, rada** + feʼl = mamnuniyat bilan, jon deb. Prídem ham, kúpim kabi, kelajakni bildiradi: kelaman.

a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-dakujem-za-pozvanie-.en: Thanks for the invitation. I'd love to come!
a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-dakujem-za-pozvanie-.t: Taklif uchun rahmat. Mamnuniyat bilan kelaman!

a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-dakujem-za-pozvanie-.en: Emma is talking about herself (ja), so the verb ends in **-m**: rada **prídem**. Prídeš goes with ty, príde with on or ona.
a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-dakujem-za-pozvanie-.t: Emma oʻzi haqida gapiryapti (ja), shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi, oʻzbekchadagi -man kabi: rada **prídem**. Prídeš — ty bilan, príde — on yoki ona bilan.

a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-mila-emma.question.en: Lucia writes Emma an e-mail. It starts “Dear Emma”. Which is right?
a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-mila-emma.question.t: Lusiya Emmaga elektron xat yozyapti. Xat «Qadrli Emma» bilan boshlanadi. Qaysi biri toʻgʻri?

a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-mila-emma.why.en: In letters and e-mails, **milý** (kind) means dear, and it agrees like any adjective: Emma is a woman, so **Milá** Emma. To Tomáš: Milý Tomáš.
a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-mila-emma.why.t: Xat va elektron xatlarda **milý** (mehribon, yoqimli) «qadrli» degani boʻladi va har qanday sifat kabi moslashadi: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun **Milá** Emma. Tomashga: Milý Tomáš.

a2-u3-pozvanka.build-lucia-ide-na-vianoc.en: Lucia is going home for Christmas.

en: Going home answers “where to?”, so it's **domov**. Doma is being at home: Som doma.
Lucia is one person (ona), so ísť is **ide**. Idú is for oni.
t: Uyga borish «qayerga?» savoliga javob beradi, shuning uchun **domov** (uyga). Doma — uyda boʻlish: Som doma. = Uydaman.
Lusiya — bir kishi (ona), shuning uchun ísť — **ide**. Idú — oni uchun.

a2-u3-pozvanka.silvester-a-novy-rok.en.en: New Year's Eve and New Year's Day
a2-u3-pozvanka.silvester-a-novy-rok.en.t: Yangi yil kechasi va Yangi yil kuni

a2-u3-pozvanka.silvester-a-novy-rok.note.en: **Silvester** is 31 December, named after the saint of that day; **Nový rok** is 1 January. Lucia invites Tomáš for Silvester too.
a2-u3-pozvanka.silvester-a-novy-rok.note.t: **Silvester** — 31-dekabr, shu kunning avliyosi nomi bilan atalgan; **Nový rok** — 1-yanvar. Lusiya Silvesterga Tomashni ham taklif qiladi.

a2-u3-pozvanka.build-dakujem-za-pozvanie.en: Thanks for the invitation, but I can't come.
a2-u3-pozvanka.build-dakujem-za-pozvanie.t: Taklif uchun rahmat, lekin kela olmayman.

en: Tomáš is talking about himself (ja), so môcť is **nemôžem**. Nemôžeš goes with ty.
After nemôžem comes the infinitive, the -ť form: nemôžem **prísť**.
t: Tomash oʻzi haqida gapiryapti (ja), shuning uchun môcť — **nemôžem**. Nemôžeš — ty bilan.
nemôžem dan keyin infinitív, yaʼni -ť shakli keladi: nemôžem **prísť** (kela olmayman).

a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-tomas-nemoze-prist.en: Tomáš can't come for New Year's Eve: he'll be with his parents in Košice. What does Lucia say?
a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-tomas-nemoze-prist.t: Tomash Yangi yil kechasiga kela olmaydi: u Koshitseda ota-onasi bilan boʻladi. Lusiya nima deydi?

a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-tomas-nemoze-prist.en: **To je škoda!** (what a pity) is for news you're sorry to hear. Teší ma is for meeting someone.
a2-u3-pozvanka.choice-tomas-nemoze-prist.t: **To je škoda!** (Attang! Afsus!) eshitib afsuslangan xabarga aytiladi. Teší ma — tanishganda aytiladi.

a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-na-silvester-budem.e.en: I'll be in Košice on New Year's Eve.

a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-na-silvester-budem.w.en: New Year's Eve is still to come, so byť takes its future form: **budem**. Som is now, bol the past.
a2-u3-pozvanka.fill-na-silvester-budem.w.t: Yangi yil kechasi hali oldinda, shuning uchun byť kelasi zamon shaklida keladi: **budem** (boʻlaman). Som — hozir, bol — oʻtgan zamon.

a2-u3-pozvanka.build-tesim-sa-na-teba.pr.en: I'm looking forward to seeing you!

en: After a preposition like na, a pronoun takes its long form: na **teba**. Ťa is the short form.
**Tešiť sa na** takes the object form, and its long form is **teba**.
t: na kabi predlogdan keyin olmosh uzun shaklda keladi: na **teba**. Ťa — qisqa shakl.
**Tešiť sa na** toʻldiruvchi shaklini talab qiladi (oʻzbekchada «…ni intiqlik bilan kutmoq»), uning uzun shakli esa **teba**.

a2-u3-pozvanka.speak-chces-prist-k-nam.e.en: Do you want to come to us for Christmas?

a2-u3-rodina.babka-a-dedko.note.en: Lucia is showing Emma photos of her family. Formally they're **stará mama** and **starý otec**, together the **starí rodičia** (grandparents). Babka Helena, Lucia's dad's mum, lives with the family.
a2-u3-rodina.babka-a-dedko.note.t: Lusiya Emmaga oilasining suratlarini koʻrsatyapti. Rasmiy tilda ular **stará mama** va **starý otec**, ikkalasi birga — **starí rodičia** (bobo-buvi). Helena buvi — Lusiyaning dadasining onasi, oila bilan birga yashaydi.

a2-u3-rodina.ujo-a-teta.note.en: Ujo Pavol is Lucia's mum's brother, and teta Mirka is his wife. A dad's brother is properly **strýko**, but many Slovaks say ujo for both.
a2-u3-rodina.ujo-a-teta.note.t: Pavol togʻa — Lusiyaning oyisining ukasi, Mirka yanga — uning xotini. Dadaning ukasi (amaki) aslida **strýko**, lekin koʻp slovaklar ikkalasini ham ujo deyishadi. Teta esa xola ham, amma ham, yanga ham boʻla oladi.

a2-u3-rodina.fill-ujo-pavol-je-mamin.why.en: **Mamin** (Mum's) is made like Luciin: mama drops -a and adds -in. Brat is masculine, so no ending: **mamin** brat. Mamina goes with a feminine word.
a2-u3-rodina.fill-ujo-pavol-je-mamin.why.t: **Mamin** (oyimning) Luciin kabi yasaladi: mama -a ni tashlab, -in qoʻshadi. Brat erkak jinsida, shuning uchun qoʻshimcha yoʻq: **mamin** brat. Mamina ayol jinsidagi soʻz bilan keladi.

a2-u3-rodina.bratranec-a-sesternica.note.en: Samko, the son of ujo Pavol and teta Mirka, is Lucia's **bratranec**. He's eight.
a2-u3-rodina.bratranec-a-sesternica.note.t: Samko — Pavol togʻa va Mirka yanganing oʻgʻli, Lusiyaning togʻavachchasi: **bratranec**. U sakkiz yoshda. Slovak tilida qaysi tomondan ekani farq qilmaydi: amakivachcha, togʻavachcha, xolavachcha, ammavachcha — oʻgʻil boʻlsa bratranec, qiz boʻlsa sesternica.

a2-u3-rodina.fill-samko-je-luciin.why.en: Samko is the son of Lucia's uncle, so he's her cousin, and a boy: **bratranec**. A girl cousin is a sesternica.
a2-u3-rodina.fill-samko-je-luciin.why.t: Samko — Lusiyaning togʻasining oʻgʻli, yaʼni togʻavachchasi, oʻzi esa oʻgʻil bola: **bratranec**. Qiz boʻlsa — sesternica.

a2-u3-rodina.vnuk-a-vnucka.note.en: Lucia is babka Helena's **vnučka**, and Marek is her **vnuk**. Grandchildren together: **vnúčatá**.
a2-u3-rodina.vnuk-a-vnucka.note.t: Lusiya — Helena buvining nevara qizi, **vnučka**, Marek esa nevara oʻgʻli, **vnuk**. Oʻzbekchada bitta soʻz, slovakchada ikkita. Nevaralar birgalikda: **vnúčatá**.

a2-u3-rodina.synovec-a-neter.note.en: To ujo Pavol, Lucia is a **neter**. To Lucia's mum, Samko is a **synovec**.
a2-u3-rodina.synovec-a-neter.note.t: Pavol togʻa uchun Lusiya — jiyan qiz, **neter**. Lusiyaning oyisi uchun Samko — jiyan oʻgʻil, **synovec**.

a2-u3-rodina.choice-kto-je-samko-mame.qu.en: Samko is the son of Lucia's mum's brother. What is he to Lucia's mum?
a2-u3-rodina.choice-kto-je-samko-mame.qu.t: Samko — Lusiyaning oyisi ukasining oʻgʻli. U Lusiyaning oyisiga kim boʻladi?

a2-u3-rodina.choice-kto-je-samko-mame.wh.en: The son of your brother or sister is your **synovec** (nephew). To Lucia he's a bratranec, a cousin; a vnuk is a grandson.
a2-u3-rodina.choice-kto-je-samko-mame.wh.t: Aka-ukangiz yoki opa-singlingizning oʻgʻli — jiyaningiz, **synovec**. Lusiyaga u bratranec (togʻavachcha), vnuk esa nevara oʻgʻil.

en: **Otcov** (Dad's) agrees with mama, a feminine word, so it adds **-a**: otcov**a** mama.
Mamina means Mum's. Babka Helena is Dad's mum: otec drops its e and adds -ov, **otcova**.
t: **Otcov** (dadamning) mama soʻziga moslashadi, u esa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **-a** qoʻshiladi: otcov**a** mama.
Mamina — oyimning. Helena buvi esa dadamning onasi: otec e ni tashlab, -ov qoʻshadi: **otcova**.

a2-u3-rodina.pribuzny.note.en: Plural: **príbuzní**. Na Vianoce prídu príbuzní. = Relatives are coming for Christmas.
a2-u3-rodina.pribuzny.note.t: Koʻplikda: **príbuzní**. Na Vianoce prídu príbuzní. = Rojdestvoga qarindoshlar keladi.

en: Lucia is Grandma's granddaughter and Marek is her grandson.
t: Lusiya buvining nevara qizi, Marek esa uning nevara oʻgʻli.
Lusiya buvining nevarasi, Marek ham uning nevarasi.
Lusiya buvining nevara qizi, Marek esa nevara oʻgʻli.

a2-u3-rodina.matka-mama-mamka.note.en: **Matka** is formal, for forms and the news; at home it's **mama** or **mamka**. Dad is **otec**, and daddy **ocko**.
a2-u3-rodina.matka-mama-mamka.note.t: **Matka** — rasmiy soʻz, anketalar va yangiliklar uchun; uyda esa **mama** yoki **mamka**. Ota — **otec**, dadajon esa — **ocko**.

a2-u3-rodina.choice-formal-matka.questio.en: Lucia is filling in a form. Which word for “mother” does the form use?
a2-u3-rodina.choice-formal-matka.questio.t: Lusiya anketa toʻldiryapti. Anketada «ona» uchun qaysi soʻz ishlatiladi?

a2-u3-rodina.choice-formal-matka.why.en: **Matka** is the formal word, the one on forms. Mamka is what you call your mum at home, and ocko means daddy.
a2-u3-rodina.choice-formal-matka.why.t: **Matka** — rasmiy soʻz, anketalarda shu yoziladi. Mamka — uyda oyiga erkalab aytiladi, ocko esa — dadajon.

a2-u3-rodina.fill-moji-rodicia-byvaju.wh.en: Rodičia is plural (oni), so the verb ends in **-ajú**: bývajú. Býva is for one person, bývam for ja.
a2-u3-rodina.fill-moji-rodicia-byvaju.wh.t: Rodičia — koʻplik (oni), shuning uchun feʼl **-ajú** bilan tugaydi: bývajú. Býva — bir kishi uchun, bývam — ja uchun.

en: The family is what you have, the object, so the adjective changes -á to **-ú**: veľk**ú**.
As the object, rodina changes -a to **-u**: mám **rodinu**.
t: Oila — sizda bor narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun sifatda -á oʻrniga **-ú** keladi: veľk**ú**.
Toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda rodina soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: mám **rodinu**.

a2-u3-vyzor.ako-vyzera.note.en: **vyzerať** = to look (like): vyzerám, vyzeráš, vyzerá… Your face is your **tvár**.
a2-u3-vyzor.ako-vyzera.note.t: **vyzerať** = koʻrinmoq, koʻrinishga ega boʻlmoq: vyzerám, vyzeráš, vyzerá… Yuz — **tvár**.

a2-u3-vyzor.fuzy.note.en: Always plural, like vlasy: Pán Kováč má sivé **fúzy**. (**sivý** = grey)
a2-u3-vyzor.fuzy.note.t: Doim koʻplikda, vlasy kabi: Pán Kováč má sivé **fúzy**. = Janob Kovachning moʻylovi oqargan. (**sivý** = kulrang, oqargan)

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-lucia-ma-dlhe.en.en: Lucia has long dark hair and wears glasses.
a2-u3-vyzor.fill-lucia-ma-dlhe.en.t: Lusiyaning uzun qora sochlari bor, u koʻzoynak taqadi.

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-tomas-ma-ciernu.en.en: Tomáš has a short black beard.

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-tomas-ma-ciernu.why.en: The beard is what Tomáš has, the object, so brada changes -a to **-u**, and its adjectives -á to -ú: krátk**u** čiern**u** brad**u**.
a2-u3-vyzor.fill-tomas-ma-ciernu.why.t: Soqol — Tomashda bor narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun brada soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u**, sifatlarida esa -á oʻrniga -ú keladi: krátk**u** čiern**u** brad**u**.

a2-u3-vyzor.nizky.note.en: The opposite of **vysoký** (tall): Babka je **nízka**, ale Marek je vysoký.
a2-u3-vyzor.nizky.note.t: **vysoký** (baland boʻyli) soʻzining teskarisi: Babka je **nízka**, ale Marek je vysoký. = Buvi past boʻyli, Marek esa baland.

a2-u3-vyzor.stihly.note.en: The opposite, **tučný** (fat), isn't polite about people: Ten kapor je veľký a tučný! Your build is your **postava**: Má štíhlu postavu.
a2-u3-vyzor.stihly.note.t: Teskarisi — **tučný** (semiz), lekin odam haqida aytilsa, odobsiz eshitiladi: Ten kapor je veľký a tučný! = Bu karp katta va semiz ekan! Qaddi-qomat — **postava**: Má štíhlu postavu. = Qomati xipcha.

en: Uncle Pavol is tall and has a beard.
Uncle Pavol is short and has a beard.
Uncle Pavol is tall and wears glasses.
t: Pavol togʻa baland boʻyli, soqoli bor.
Pavol togʻa past boʻyli, soqoli bor.
Pavol togʻa baland boʻyli, koʻzoynak taqadi.

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-babka-je-nizka.why.en: Babka is feminine: **nízka**. The ending is a short -a, not -á, because the syllable before it is long (í), and Slovak avoids two long syllables in a row.
a2-u3-vyzor.fill-babka-je-nizka.why.t: Babka ayol jinsida: **nízka**. Qoʻshimcha -á emas, qisqa -a, chunki oldingi boʻgʻin choʻziq (í), slovak tili esa ikki choʻziq boʻgʻinni ketma-ket qoʻyishdan qochadi.

a2-u3-vyzor.kuceravy.note.en: Marek má krátke **kučeravé** vlasy. Red hair is **ryšavé** vlasy; fair hair is **blond**, which never changes its ending.
a2-u3-vyzor.kuceravy.note.t: Marek má krátke **kučeravé** vlasy. = Marekning sochi kalta va jingalak. Malla soch — **ryšavé** vlasy; sariq soch — **blond**, bu soʻzning qoʻshimchasi hech qachon oʻzgarmaydi.

a2-u3-vyzor.build-kto-je-ten-pan.prompt.en: Who's that man with the beard?

en: After **s** (with) comes the instrumental: brada → s brad**ou**.
Pán is masculine, so “that” is **ten**. Tá goes with feminine words: tá pani.
t: **s** (bilan) dan keyin inštrumentál keladi: brada → s brad**ou** (soqol bilan).
Pán erkak jinsida, shuning uchun «anavi» — **ten**. Tá ayol jinsidagi soʻzlar bilan keladi: tá pani.

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-ta-pani-s-rysavymi.en.en: Who's that lady with the red hair?

a2-u3-vyzor.fill-ta-pani-s-rysavymi.why.en: After **s** (with), plural words take the instrumental, and adjectives end in **-ými**: s ryšav**ými** vlasmi.
a2-u3-vyzor.fill-ta-pani-s-rysavymi.why.t: **s** (bilan) dan keyin koʻplikdagi soʻzlar inštrumentálda keladi, sifatlar esa **-ými** bilan tugaydi: s ryšav**ými** vlasmi.

a2-u3-vyzor.choice-liam-je-vysoky.questi.en: Emma's brother Liam is fifteen, tall and slim. Which sentence says so?
a2-u3-vyzor.choice-liam-je-vysoky.questi.t: Emmaning ukasi Liam oʻn besh yoshda, baland boʻyli va xipcha. Qaysi gap shuni aytadi?

a2-u3-vyzor.speak-ako-vyzera-tvoj.en.en: What does your cousin look like?

a2-u3-povaha.vazny-a-vtipny.note.en: Ujo Pavol is never **vážny**: he's vtipný and tells jokes all evening. **Taký, taká, také** = so, such: Prečo si dnes taký vážny?
a2-u3-povaha.vazny-a-vtipny.note.t: Pavol togʻa hech qachon **vážny** emas: u vtipný, kech boʻyi latifa aytib beradi. **Taký, taká, také** = shunchalik, buncha: Prečo si dnes taký vážny? = Bugun nega buncha jiddiysan?

a2-u3-povaha.smiat-sa.note.en: smejem sa, smeješ sa, smeje sa… Ujo Pavol sa veľa **smeje**. Laughter is **smiech**.
a2-u3-povaha.smiat-sa.note.t: smejem sa, smeješ sa, smeje sa… Ujo Pavol sa veľa **smeje**. = Pavol togʻa koʻp kuladi. Kulgi — **smiech**.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-babka-je-ticha.why.en: Babka is feminine, so the adjective ends in **-á**: tich**á**, like mil**á**.
a2-u3-povaha.fill-babka-je-ticha.why.t: Babka ayol jinsida, shuning uchun sifat **-á** bilan tugaydi: tich**á**, mil**á** kabi.

a2-u3-povaha.hlucny.note.en: The opposite of **tichý** (quiet). Pán Kováč nemá rád **hlučnú** hudbu. = Mr Kováč doesn't like loud music.
a2-u3-povaha.hlucny.note.t: **tichý** (jim, kamgap) soʻzining teskarisi. Pán Kováč nemá rád **hlučnú** hudbu. = Janob Kovach shovqinli musiqani yoqtirmaydi.

a2-u3-povaha.build-samko-nie-je-hanblivy.en: Samko isn't shy, he's very loud.
a2-u3-povaha.build-samko-nie-je-hanblivy.t: Samko uyatchan emas, u juda shovqinli.

en: Samko is a boy, so the adjective ends in **-ý**: hanblivý. Hanblivá is for a woman or a girl.
Loud is **hlučný**. Tichý means quiet, the opposite.
t: Samko — oʻgʻil bola, shuning uchun sifat **-ý** bilan tugaydi: hanblivý. Hanblivá — ayol yoki qiz uchun.

en: Marek works hard, he isn't lazy.
Marek is lazy, he doesn't work.

a2-u3-povaha.pokojny.note.en: Someone lively and hot-tempered is **temperamentný**: Teta Mirka je temperamentná, ujo Pavol je pokojný.
a2-u3-povaha.pokojny.note.t: Jonli va qiziqqon odam — **temperamentný**: Teta Mirka je temperamentná, ujo Pavol je pokojný. = Mirka yanga qiziqqon, Pavol togʻa esa xotirjam.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-a-ujo-su.en.en: Aunt Mirka and Uncle Pavol are very friendly.
a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-a-ujo-su.en.t: Mirka yanga va Pavol togʻa juda samimiy.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-a-ujo-su.why.en: A woman and a man together count as men, so the adjective takes the men's plural **-í**: priateľsk**í**.
a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-a-ujo-su.why.t: Ayol va erkak birga erkaklar kabi hisoblanadi, shuning uchun sifat erkaklar koʻpligi qoʻshimchasi **-í** ni oladi: priateľsk**í**.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-preco-si-taky.en.en: Why are you so serious, Samko?

a2-u3-povaha.fill-preco-si-taky.why.en: **Taký** (so) changes like an adjective. Samko is a boy, so it's tak**ý**, like vážn**y**.
a2-u3-povaha.fill-preco-si-taky.why.t: **Taký** (buncha) sifat kabi oʻzgaradi. Samko — oʻgʻil bola, shuning uchun tak**ý**, vážn**y** kabi.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-mirka-sa-smeje.en.en: Aunt Mirka is cheerful and laughs a lot.

a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-mirka-sa-smeje.wh.en: Teta Mirka is ona, so the verb has no ending: **smeje** sa. Smejem goes with ja, smejú with oni.
a2-u3-povaha.fill-teta-mirka-sa-smeje.wh.t: Mirka yanga — ona, shuning uchun feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: **smeje** sa. Smejem — ja bilan, smejú — oni bilan.

a2-u3-povaha.choice-teta-mirka-je.questi.en: Teta Mirka laughs a lot, talks fast and is full of energy. Which word fits her?
a2-u3-povaha.choice-teta-mirka-je.questi.t: Mirka yanga koʻp kuladi, tez gapiradi va gʻayratga toʻla. Qaysi soʻz unga mos keladi?

a2-u3-povaha.build-preco-si-taka-smutna..en: Why are you so sad, Lucia?

en: Lucia is a woman, so taký takes the feminine ending: **taká**, like smutná.
Lucia is a woman, so the adjective ends in **-á**: smutn**á**.
t: Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun taký ayol jinsi qoʻshimchasini oladi: **taká**, smutná kabi.
Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun sifat **-á** bilan tugaydi: smutn**á**.

en: Uncle Pavol is very funny and good fun.
Uncle Pavol is very funny and fun.
t: Pavol togʻa juda hazilkash va xushchaqchaq.
Pavol togʻa juda hazilkash va qiziqchi.
Pavol togʻa juda hazilkash va quvnoq odam.

en: To compare, add **-ší** when one consonant comes before the ending: mlad-ý → mlad**ší**, tich-ý → tich**ší** (ch is one letter). After two or more, add **-ejší**: siln-ý → siln**ejší**, vážn-y → vážn**ejší**.
Adjectives in -ký and -oký drop the k (or ok), and s, z become š, ž: vysoký → vy**šší**, nízky → ni**žší**.
The endings: **-í** for him, **-ia** for her, **-ie** for it: starš**í** brat, starš**ia** sestra, starš**ie** dieťa.
t: Taqqoslash uchun, qoʻshimchadan oldin bitta undosh boʻlsa, **-ší** qoʻshiladi: mlad-ý → mlad**ší**, tich-ý → tich**ší** (ch — bitta harf). Ikki yoki undan ortiq undosh boʻlsa, **-ejší**: siln-ý → siln**ejší**, vážn-y → vážn**ejší**. Bu oʻzbekchadagi -roq ga oʻxshaydi: yosh → yoshroq.
-ký va -oký bilan tugaydigan sifatlarda k (yoki ok) tushib qoladi, s va z esa š va ž ga aylanadi: vysoký → vy**šší**, nízky → ni**žší**.
Qoʻshimchalar: erkak jinsi uchun **-í**, ayol jinsi uchun **-ia**, oʻrta jins uchun **-ie**: starš**í** brat (aka), starš**ia** sestra (opa), starš**ie** dieťa (kattaroq bola).

en: “Than” is **ako** or **než**. Both are right; ako is more common: Marek je starší **ako** Lucia.
To say by how much, use **o** and the object form: Marek je **o** deväť rokov starší. Emma je staršia **o** dva roky.
t: Taqqoslashdagi «…dan» slovakchada alohida soʻz: **ako** yoki **než**. Ikkalasi ham toʻgʻri; ako koʻproq ishlatiladi: Marek je starší **ako** Lucia. = Marek Lusiyadan katta. Bu misolda ako dan keyingi soʻz asosiy shaklda qoladi.
Qanchaga farq qilishini aytish uchun **o** va toʻldiruvchi shakli ishlatiladi: Marek je **o** deväť rokov starší. = Marek toʻqqiz yosh katta. Emma je staršia **o** dva roky.

en: Marek is nine years older than Lucia.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-marek-je-starsi.why.en: Marek is a man, so the comparative ends in **-í**: starš**í**. Staršia is for a woman, staršie for a thing.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-marek-je-starsi.why.t: Marek — erkak, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-í** bilan tugaydi: starš**í**. Staršia — ayol uchun, staršie — oʻrta jinsdagi soʻz uchun.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-lucia-je-mladsia.why.en: Lucia is a woman, so the comparative ends in **-ia**: mladš**ia**.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-lucia-je-mladsia.why.t: Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-ia** bilan tugaydi: mladš**ia**.

en: Emma is a woman, so the comparative ends in **-ia**: starš**ia**.
Older is **staršia**, from starý. Mladšia means younger.
t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-ia** bilan tugaydi: starš**ia**.
Katta — **staršia**, starý dan. Mladšia — kichik, yoshroq.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-babka-je-tichsia.why.en: Tichý has one consonant (ch) before the ending, so it takes **-ší**, and babka is a woman: tich**šia**.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-babka-je-tichsia.why.t: Tichý soʻzida qoʻshimchadan oldin bitta undosh (ch) bor, shuning uchun **-ší** oladi, babka esa ayol: tich**šia**.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-samko-je-hlucnejsi.why.en: Hlučný has two consonants (čn) before the ending, so it takes **-ejší**, and Samko is a boy: hlučn**ejší**.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-samko-je-hlucnejsi.why.t: Hlučný soʻzida qoʻshimchadan oldin ikki undosh (čn) bor, shuning uchun **-ejší** oladi, Samko esa oʻgʻil bola: hlučn**ejší**.

a2-u3-starsi.choice-marek-o-devat-rokov..en: Marek is 28 and Lucia is 19. Which is true?
a2-u3-starsi.choice-marek-o-devat-rokov..t: Marek 28 yoshda, Lusiya esa 19 yoshda. Qaysi biri toʻgʻri?

a2-u3-starsi.choice-marek-o-devat-rokov..en: Marek is the elder, so he's **starší**, and **o** deväť rokov says by how much.
a2-u3-starsi.choice-marek-o-devat-rokov..t: Marek katta, shuning uchun u **starší**, **o** deväť rokov esa qanchaga ekanini aytadi.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-emma-je-o-dva-roky.en.en: Emma is two years older than Lucia.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-emma-je-o-dva-roky.why.en: By how much is **o** + the object form: **o** dva roky.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-emma-je-o-dva-roky.why.t: Qanchaga farq qilishi — **o** + toʻldiruvchi shakli: **o** dva roky (ikki yoshga).

a2-u3-starsi.build-tomas-je-o-dva-roky.p.en: Tomáš is two years older than Marek.

en: Tomáš is a man, so the comparative ends in **-í**: starš**í**.
By how much is **o**: o dva roky.
t: Tomash — erkak, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-í** bilan tugaydi: starš**í**.
Qanchaga farq qilishi — **o**: o dva roky.

a2-u3-starsi.fill-tomas-je-vyssi.why.en: Vysoký drops -ok- and s becomes š: vy**šší**. Tomáš is a man, so it ends in -í.
a2-u3-starsi.fill-tomas-je-vyssi.why.t: Vysoký soʻzida -ok- tushib qoladi, s esa š ga aylanadi: vy**šší**. Tomash — erkak, shuning uchun -í bilan tugaydi.

en: The train is faster than the bus.
A train is faster than a bus.

a2-u3-darceky.roman-a-detektivka.en.en: a novel and a detective story

a2-u3-darceky.roman-a-detektivka.note.en: Emma and Lucia are buying presents. Lucia's mum loves **detektívky**, babka likes **romány**, and Dad likes **ľudová hudba**, folk music.
a2-u3-darceky.roman-a-detektivka.note.t: Emma va Lusiya sovgʻa xarid qilyapti. Lusiyaning oyisi detektivlarni (**detektívky**) yaxshi koʻradi, buvisi romanlarni (**romány**), dadasi esa xalq musiqasini (**ľudová hudba**).

a2-u3-darceky.fill-ten-roman-je-pre.why.en: **Pre** (for) takes the object form: babka → pre babk**u**.
a2-u3-darceky.fill-ten-roman-je-pre.why.t: **Pre** (uchun) toʻldiruvchi shaklini talab qiladi: babka → pre babk**u**.

a2-u3-darceky.sal-a-rukavice.note.en: Shopping is a **nákup**. Gloves come in pairs, so you mostly say **rukavice** (one glove is a rukavica). Warm slippers are **teplé papuče**.
a2-u3-darceky.sal-a-rukavice.note.t: Xarid — **nákup**. Qoʻlqoplar juft boʻladi, shuning uchun koʻpincha **rukavice** deyiladi (bitta qoʻlqop — rukavica). Issiq shippak — **teplé papuče**.

a2-u3-darceky.fill-emma-a-lucia-idu-na.e.en: Emma and Lucia are going shopping.

a2-u3-darceky.fill-emma-a-lucia-idu-na.w.en: Going somewhere is **na** + the object form, and nákup (shopping) is a masculine thing, so it doesn't change: na **nákup**.
a2-u3-darceky.fill-emma-a-lucia-idu-na.w.t: Biror joyga borish — **na** + toʻldiruvchi shakli, nákup (xarid) esa erkak jinsidagi jonsiz narsa, shuning uchun oʻzgarmaydi: na **nákup**.

a2-u3-darceky.fill-tento-sal-je-lacnejsi.en: This scarf is cheaper than that one.
Šál is masculine, so the comparative ends in **-í**: lacnejš**í**.
a2-u3-darceky.fill-tento-sal-je-lacnejsi.t: Šál erkak jinsida, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-í** bilan tugaydi: lacnejš**í**.

en: Rukavice is plural and a thing, so the comparative ends in **-ie**: lacnejš**ie** rukavice.
Gloves come in pairs: **rukavice**. Rukavica is one glove.
t: Rukavice — koʻplikdagi jonsiz narsa, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-ie** bilan tugaydi: lacnejš**ie** rukavice.
Qoʻlqoplar juft boʻladi: **rukavice**. Rukavica — bitta qoʻlqop.

a2-u3-darceky.choice-je-mi-luto-ten-sal..en: What does the shop assistant mean?

en: Sorry, that scarf isn't for sale.
I'm sorry, that scarf is too expensive.
I'm sorry, we don't have that scarf any more.
t: Afsuski, bu sharf bizda boshqa qolmadi.

a2-u3-darceky.vymenit.note.en: Lucia bought Dad a sweater last week, but it's too small. Môžem ten sveter **vymeniť**? = Can I exchange this sweater?
a2-u3-darceky.vymenit.note.t: Lusiya oʻtgan hafta dadasiga sviter olgan edi, lekin u juda kichik ekan. Môžem ten sveter **vymeniť**? = Bu sviterni almashtirsam boʻladimi?

a2-u3-darceky.fill-mozem-ten-sveter.why.en: After **môžem** comes the infinitive, the -ť form: môžem **vymeniť**.
a2-u3-darceky.fill-mozem-ten-sveter.why.t: **môžem** dan keyin infinitív, yaʼni -ť shakli keladi: môžem **vymeniť**.

a2-u3-darceky.omyl.note.en: Prepáčte, to je asi **omyl**. = Sorry, that must be a mistake. (**asi** = probably)
a2-u3-darceky.omyl.note.t: Prepáčte, to je asi **omyl**. = Kechirasiz, bu xato boʻlsa kerak. (**asi** = ehtimol, shekilli)

a2-u3-darceky.build-prepacte-to-je-asi.p.en: Excuse me, that's probably a mistake.

en: You say vy to a shop assistant, so it's **Prepáčte**. Prepáč is for a friend.
“That is” is to **je**. Som goes with ja.
t: Sotuvchiga vy (siz) deysiz, shuning uchun **Prepáčte**. Prepáč — doʻstga.

a2-u3-darceky.fill-otec-ma-rad-ludovu.wh.en: Music is what Dad likes, the object, so ľudová changes -á to **-ú**, just as hudba → hudbu.
a2-u3-darceky.fill-otec-ma-rad-ludovu.wh.t: Musiqa — dadam yaxshi koʻradigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun ľudová soʻzida -á oʻrniga **-ú** keladi, xuddi hudba → hudbu kabi.

en: Mum likes to read detective stories.
Five everyday adjectives change completely. Learn them as words. **zlý** = bad.
They end like any comparative: lepš**í** darček, lepš**ia** kniha, lepš**ie** auto.
t: Beshta kundalik sifatning qiyosiy darajasi butunlay boshqacha. Ularni alohida soʻz sifatida yodlang. **zlý** = yomon.
Qoʻshimchalari boshqa qiyosiy darajalar kabi: lepš**í** darček, lepš**ia** kniha, lepš**ie** auto.

en: For “the most”, add **naj-** to the comparative: starší → **naj**starší, lepší → **naj**lepší. You know one already: Všetko **naj**lepšie! = All the best!
To say “in”, use v or na with the locative: najstarší **v rodine** (the oldest in the family), najväčšie mesto **na Slovensku**.
t: Oʻzbekchadagi «eng» oʻrniga qiyosiy darajaga **naj-** qoʻshiladi: starší → **naj**starší (eng katta), lepší → **naj**lepší (eng yaxshi). Bittasini allaqachon bilasiz: Všetko **naj**lepšie! (soʻzma-soʻz: hammasi eng yaxshi).
«…dagi eng …» deyish uchun v yoki na + lokál (oʻrin-payt kelishigi) ishlatiladi: najstarší **v rodine** (oiladagi eng katta), najväčšie mesto **na Slovensku** (Slovakiyadagi eng katta shahar).

en: Grandma is the oldest in the family.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-tento-sal-je-krajsi..en: This scarf is nicer than the green one.
Pekný has an irregular comparative, **krajší**. Šál is masculine, so it ends in -í.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-tento-sal-je-krajsi..t: Pekný ning qiyosiy darajasi — istisno: **krajší**. Šál erkak jinsida, shuning uchun -í bilan tugaydi.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-potrebujem-mensie.en.en: Those gloves are too big. I need smaller ones.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-potrebujem-mensie.en.t: Bu qoʻlqoplar katta. Menga kichikrogʻi kerak.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-potrebujem-mensie.wh.en: Too big, so you need smaller: malý → **menší**, and rukavice is a plural thing, so **menšie**.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-potrebujem-mensie.wh.t: Juda katta, demak sizga kichikroq kerak: malý → **menší**, rukavice esa koʻplikdagi jonsiz narsa, shuning uchun **menšie**.

a2-u3-najlepsi.choice-opposite-lepsi.que.en: Which word is the opposite of lepší (better)?

a2-u3-najlepsi.choice-opposite-lepsi.why.en: Lepší comes from dobrý; its opposite, worse, comes from zlý: **horší**. Both are irregular.
a2-u3-najlepsi.choice-opposite-lepsi.why.t: Lepší dobrý dan yasalgan; uning teskarisi, «yomonroq», zlý dan: **horší**. Ikkalasi ham istisno.

en: Darček is masculine, so it's najlepš**í**.
The best of all takes **naj-**: **naj**lepší. Lepší is just better.
t: Darček erkak jinsida, shuning uchun najlepš**í**.
Hammasidan yaxshi — **naj-** bilan: **naj**lepší. Lepší — shunchaki yaxshiroq.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-samko-je-najmladsi.e.en: Samko is the youngest in the family.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-samko-je-najmladsi.w.en: The youngest of all takes **naj-**, and Samko is a boy: **naj**mladší.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-samko-je-najmladsi.w.t: Hammasidan kichik — **naj-** bilan, Samko esa oʻgʻil bola: **naj**mladší.

a2-u3-najlepsi.choice-ktore-mesto-je-naj.en: Samko is quizzing Emma. What's the answer?
a2-u3-najlepsi.choice-ktore-mesto-je-naj.t: Samko Emmaga viktorina savollarini beryapti. Javob qaysi?

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-co-je-vacsie.en.en: Which is bigger: Žilina or Košice?
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-co-je-vacsie.en.t: Qaysi biri kattaroq: Jilinami yoki Koshitsemi?

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-co-je-vacsie.why.en: After **čo** (what), the adjective is neuter: čo je väčš**ie**? Veľký → väčší is irregular.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-co-je-vacsie.why.t: **čo** (nima) dan keyin sifat oʻrta jinsda keladi: čo je väčš**ie**? Veľký → väčší — istisno.

en: Košice is a plural word in Slovak, so byť is **sú**.
Košice is plural and not a group of men, so the comparative ends in **-ie**: väčš**ie**.
t: Slovak tilida Košice — koʻplikdagi soʻz, shuning uchun byť — **sú**.
Košice — koʻplik, lekin erkaklar guruhi emas, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-ie** bilan tugaydi: väčš**ie**.

a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-februar-je-najkratsi.en: Krátky drops its k (and á gets short): krat**ší**; the shortest takes naj-: **naj**kratší. Mesiac is masculine, so -í.
a2-u3-najlepsi.fill-februar-je-najkratsi.t: Krátky soʻzida k tushib qoladi (á esa qisqaradi): krat**ší**; eng qisqa — naj- bilan: **naj**kratší. Mesiac erkak jinsida, shuning uchun -í.

en: Marek is the best cook in the family.
You know **Páči sa mi** and **Zavolám ti**: mi and ti mean “to me, to you”. That's the dative, the to-whom case. Nouns have it too: Kúpim darček **mame**. = I'll buy Mum a present.
Ask **Komu?** (to whom?). Men take **-ovi**: otec → otc**ovi**, ujo → uj**ovi**, Marek → Marek**ovi**. Women change -a to **-e**: mama → mam**e**, babka → babk**e**.
t: **Páči sa mi** va **Zavolám ti** ni bilasiz: mi va ti — «menga, senga». Bu datív (joʻnalish kelishigi), «kimga?» kelishigi, xuddi oʻzbekchadagi -ga kabi. Otlarda ham bor: Kúpim darček **mame**. = Oyimga sovgʻa olaman.
**Komu?** (kimga?) deb soʻraladi. Erkaklar **-ovi** oladi: otec → otc**ovi**, ujo → uj**ovi**, Marek → Marek**ovi**. Ayollarda -a **-e** ga aylanadi: mama → mam**e**, babka → babk**e**.

en: Who are you buying that scarf for? – Grandma.

a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-ten-sal-babke.en.en: I'll buy that scarf for Grandma.

a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-ten-sal-babke.why.en: Grandma is the one who gets it, so she's in the dative: babk**e**. Babku would need pre: pre babku.
a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-ten-sal-babke.why.t: Sharfni buvi oladi, shuning uchun u datívda: babk**e** (buviga). Babku uchun pre kerak boʻlardi: pre babku (buvi uchun).

a2-u3-komu.fill-dam-tu-knihu-marekovi.en.en: I'll give that book to Marek.

a2-u3-komu.fill-dam-tu-knihu-marekovi.wh.en: Marek gets the book, so he's in the dative, and men add **-ovi**: Marek**ovi**. Mareka is the object form.
a2-u3-komu.fill-dam-tu-knihu-marekovi.wh.t: Kitobni Marek oladi, shuning uchun u datívda, erkaklar esa **-ovi** qoʻshadi: Marek**ovi** (Marekka). Mareka — toʻldiruvchi shakli (Marekni).

a2-u3-komu.choice-komu-koho-kto.question.en: Which question asks who gets something?
a2-u3-komu.choice-komu-koho-kto.question.t: Qaysi savol narsani kim olishini soʻraydi?

a2-u3-komu.choice-komu-koho-kto.why.en: **Komu?** (to whom?) asks for the dative. Koho? asks for the object, kto? for the subject.
a2-u3-komu.choice-komu-koho-kto.why.t: **Komu?** (kimga?) datívni soʻraydi. Koho? (kimni?) — toʻldiruvchini, kto? (kim?) — egani.

en: Dad is the one who gets the book, so he's in the dative: otec → otc**ovi**. Otca is the object form.
The book is what you buy, the object, so kniha changes -a to **-u**.
t: Kitobni dadam oladi, shuning uchun u datívda: otec → otc**ovi** (dadamga). Otca — toʻldiruvchi shakli (dadamni).
Kitob — siz oladigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun kniha soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi.

a2-u3-komu.fill-co-kupis-ujovi.en.en: What will you buy Uncle Pavol?

a2-u3-komu.fill-co-kupis-ujovi.why.en: Both words are in the dative, each with **-ovi**: **ujovi** Pavlovi.
a2-u3-komu.fill-co-kupis-ujovi.why.t: Ikkala soʻz ham datívda, har biri **-ovi** bilan: **ujovi** Pavlovi. Oʻzbekchada -ga faqat oxirgi soʻzga qoʻshiladi, slovakchada esa har biriga.

en: Women's words in **-ia** take **-ii**: Lucia → Luci**i**. After a soft letter, and in words without -a, it's **-i**: sesternica → sesternic**i**, neter → neter**i**. Neuter words take **-u**: dieťa → dieťať**u** (a child).
Adjectives take **-ému** for him or it (a comparative takes **-iemu**) and **-ej** for her. Ten becomes **tomu** and **tej**: tomu mal**ému** dieťaťu, mladš**iemu** bratovi, tej mil**ej** pani.
t: **-ia** bilan tugaydigan ayol soʻzlari **-ii** oladi: Lucia → Luci**i**. Yumshoq harfdan keyin va -a siz soʻzlarda **-i**: sesternica → sesternic**i**, neter → neter**i**. Oʻrta jinsdagi soʻzlar **-u** oladi: dieťa → dieťať**u** (bolaga).

Sifatlar erkak va oʻrta jinsda **-ému** (qiyosiy daraja **-iemu**), ayol jinsida **-ej** oladi. Ten esa **tomu** va **tej** ga aylanadi: tomu mal**ému** dieťaťu, mladš**iemu** bratovi, tej mil**ej** pani.

en: Emma will send her cousin a postcard.
I'll buy it for my younger brother.

a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-to-malemu-samkovi..en: I'll buy it for little Samko.
Samkovi is in the dative, so its adjective is too: for him, **-ému**, mal**ému** Samkovi. Malého is the object form.
a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-to-malemu-samkovi..t: Samkovi datívda, demak sifati ham datívda: erkak jinsi uchun **-ému**, mal**ému** Samkovi. Malého — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-to-starej-mame.why.en: Stará mama is grandma. Mame is feminine and in the dative, so the adjective takes **-ej**: star**ej** mame. Starú is the object form.
a2-u3-komu.fill-kupim-to-starej-mame.why.t: Stará mama — buvi. Mame ayol jinsida va datívda, shuning uchun sifat **-ej** oladi: star**ej** mame. Starú — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-zavola-sesternici.w.en: Phoning someone is zavolať + the dative. The object form, as in A1's volať Luciu, is also standard. Sesternica has a soft c before the -a, so it takes **-i**: sesternic**i**.
a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-zavola-sesternici.w.t: Kimgadir qoʻngʻiroq qilish — zavolať + datív, xuddi oʻzbekchadagi -ga kabi. A1 dagi volať Luciu kabi toʻldiruvchi shakli ham toʻgʻri hisoblanadi. Sesternica soʻzida -a dan oldin yumshoq c bor, shuning uchun **-i** oladi: sesternic**i**.

a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-sal-lucii.en.en: Emma will buy Lucia a scarf.

a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-sal-lucii.why.en: Lucia ends in -ia, so the dative is **-ii**: Luci**i**. Luciu is the object form.
a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-sal-lucii.why.t: Lucia -ia bilan tugaydi, shuning uchun datív **-ii**: Luci**i** (Lusiyaga). Luciu — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-mladsiemu.en.en: Emma will buy her younger brother a book.

a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-mladsiemu.why.en: Bratovi is in the dative, so its adjective is too, and a comparative takes **-iemu**: mladš**iemu** bratovi.
a2-u3-komu.fill-emma-kupi-mladsiemu.why.t: Bratovi datívda, demak sifati ham, qiyosiy daraja esa **-iemu** oladi: mladš**iemu** bratovi. Mladší brat — uka.

en: Samko gets the present, so he's in the dative: Samk**ovi**. Samka is the object form.
The question is to ty, so the verb ends in **-š**: kúpiš.
t: Sovgʻani Samko oladi, shuning uchun u datívda: Samk**ovi** (Samkoga). Samka — toʻldiruvchi shakli (Samkoni).
Savol ty (sen) ga berilyapti, shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: kúpiš.

a2-u3-komu.fill-ten-darcek-je-pre-mamu.w.en: After **pre** (for) comes the object form: pre mam**u**. Without pre, use the dative: Dám ho mam**e**.
a2-u3-komu.fill-ten-darcek-je-pre-mamu.w.t: **pre** (uchun) dan keyin toʻldiruvchi shakli keladi: pre mam**u**. pre boʻlmasa, datív ishlatiladi: Dám ho mam**e**. = Uni oyimga beraman.

en: Marek will buy me a book.
I'll buy a book with Marek.

a2-u3-komu.choice-kupim-marekovi-knihu.w.en: **Marekovi** is the dative: Marek is the one who gets the book. With Marek would be s Marekom.
a2-u3-komu.choice-kupim-marekovi-knihu.w.t: **Marekovi** — datív: kitobni Marek oladi. «Marek bilan» — s Marekom boʻlardi.

a2-u3-komu.fill-komu-das-tu-kavu.en.en: Who will you give that coffee to? – That man by the window.
a2-u3-komu.fill-komu-das-tu-kavu.en.t: Bu qahvani kimga berasan? — Deraza yonidagi anavi kishiga.

a2-u3-komu.fill-komu-das-tu-kavu.why.en: Pánovi is in the dative, so “that” is too: **tomu** pánovi. Toho is the object form.
a2-u3-komu.fill-komu-das-tu-kavu.why.t: Pánovi datívda, shuning uchun «anavi» ham datívda: **tomu** pánovi. Toho — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: In the plural, masculine words take **-om**: rodičia → rodič**om**, kamaráti → kamarát**om**. Feminine and neuter words take **-ám**: sestry → sestr**ám**, mestá → mest**ám**.
After a long syllable it's a short **-am**: kamarátky → kamarátk**am**. Two words have their own forms: deti → **deťom**, ľudia → **ľuďom**.
Adjectives and ten end in **-ým**: **tým** mil**ým** ľuďom, star**ým** rodičom.
t: Koʻplikda erkak jinsidagi soʻzlar **-om** oladi: rodičia → rodič**om**, kamaráti → kamarát**om**. Ayol va oʻrta jinsdagi soʻzlar **-ám** oladi: sestry → sestr**ám**, mestá → mest**ám**.
Choʻziq boʻgʻindan keyin qisqa **-am** keladi: kamarátky → kamarátk**am**. Ikki soʻzning oʻz shakli bor: deti → **deťom**, ľudia → **ľuďom**.
Sifatlar va ten **-ým** bilan tugaydi: **tým** mil**ým** ľuďom, star**ým** rodičom.

en: I'll phone my parents at Christmas.
I'll send my friends some photos.
Grandma is telling the children about Christmas.
t: Buvi bolalarga Rojdestvo haqida gapirib beryapti.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-na-vianoce-zavolam.en.en: I'll phone my parents at Christmas.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-na-vianoce-zavolam.wh.en: Phoning someone is zavolať + the dative, and masculine plurals end in **-om**: rodič**om**. Rodičoch is the locative.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-na-vianoce-zavolam.wh.t: Kimgadir qoʻngʻiroq qilish — zavolať + datív, erkak jinsidagi koʻplik esa **-om** bilan tugaydi: rodič**om**. Rodičoch — lokál.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-kupime-darceky-detom..en: The children get the presents, so they're in the dative: deti → **deťom**. Deťoch is the locative: o deťoch.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-kupime-darceky-detom..t: Sovgʻalarni bolalar oladi, shuning uchun ular datívda: deti → **deťom**. Deťoch — lokál: o deťoch (bolalar haqida).

a2-u3-rodicom.build-lucia-pise-kamaratka.en: Lucia is writing to her friends.

en: Lucia writes **to** her friends, so they're in the dative: kamarátk**am**, with a short -am after the long á.
Lucia is one person (ona), so písať is **píše**.
t: Lusiya dugonalariga yozadi, shuning uchun ular datívda: kamarátk**am**, choʻziq á dan keyin qisqa -am.
Lusiya — bir kishi (ona), shuning uchun písať — **píše**.

a2-u3-rodicom.choice-zavolam-rodicom.que.en: “I'll phone my parents.” Which is right?

a2-u3-rodicom.choice-zavolam-rodicom.why.en: Zavolať takes the dative, and rodičia becomes **rodičom**. Rodičoch is the locative.
a2-u3-rodicom.choice-zavolam-rodicom.why.t: Zavolať datívni talab qiladi, rodičia esa **rodičom** boʻladi. Rodičoch — lokál.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-dava-jablka-tym.en: Grandma gave apples to those little children.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-dava-jablka-tym.t: Buvi anavi kichkina bolalarga olma berdi.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-dava-jablka-tym.en: Deťom is in the dative plural, so “those” and the adjective are too: **tým** mal**ým** deťom.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-dava-jablka-tym.t: Deťom — koʻplikdagi datív, shuning uchun «anavi» ham, sifat ham datívda: **tým** mal**ým** deťom.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-rozprava-vnucat.en: Grandma tells her grandchildren about Christmas.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-rozprava-vnucat.t: Buvi nevaralariga Rojdestvo haqida gapirib beradi.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-rozprava-vnucat.en: Babka tells it to them, so they're in the dative: neuter -á becomes **-ám**, vnúčat**ám**.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-babka-rozprava-vnucat.t: Buvi ularga gapirib beradi, shuning uchun ular datívda: oʻrta jinsdagi -á **-ám** ga aylanadi: vnúčat**ám**.

a2-u3-rodicom.build-tomas-pise-kamaratom.en: Tomáš is writing his friends an e-mail.

en: His friends get the e-mail, so they're in the dative: kamarát**om**. Kamarátov is the object form.
Tomáš is one person (on), so písať is **píše**.
t: Elektron xatni doʻstlari oladi, shuning uchun ular datívda: kamarát**om** (doʻstlariga). Kamarátov — toʻldiruvchi shakli (doʻstlarini).
Tomash — bir kishi (on), shuning uchun písať — **píše**.

a2-u3-rodicom.fill-volame-starym-rodicom.en: Over Christmas we phone our grandparents.
Rodičom is in the dative plural, so the adjective ends in **-ým**: star**ým** rodičom.
a2-u3-rodicom.fill-volame-starym-rodicom.t: Rodičom — koʻplikdagi datív, shuning uchun sifat **-ým** bilan tugaydi: star**ým** rodičom.

en: Grandma ate apples with the children.

a2-u3-rodicom.choice-babka-dala-detom.wh.en: **Deťom** is the dative plural: the children get the apples. Babka is the subject, the one who gives.
a2-u3-rodicom.choice-babka-dala-detom.wh.t: **Deťom** — koʻplikdagi datív: olmani bolalar oladi. Babka — ega, yaʼni beruvchi.

en: I'll send photos to my parents.
I'll send my parents some photos.

a2-u3-navsteva.vitajte-u-nas.note.en: Emma and Lucia arrive in Žilina by train. **u nás** = at our place. Lucia's mum says vitajte to both girls; to one friend: Vitaj u nás!
a2-u3-navsteva.vitajte-u-nas.note.t: Emma va Lusiya Jilinaga poyezdda keladi. **u nás** = biznikida, bizning uyda. Lusiyaning oyisi ikkala qizga vitajte deydi; bitta doʻstga: Vitaj u nás! = Xush kelibsan!

a2-u3-navsteva.choice-mama-otvara-dvere..en: Lucia's mum opens the door to Lucia and Emma. What does she say?
a2-u3-navsteva.choice-mama-otvara-dvere..t: Lusiyaning oyisi Lusiya va Emmaga eshikni ochadi. U nima deydi?

a2-u3-navsteva.choice-mama-otvara-dvere..en: She's welcoming two people, so she uses the vy form: **Vitajte**. Vitaj is for one friend.
a2-u3-navsteva.choice-mama-otvara-dvere..t: U ikki kishini kutib olyapti, shuning uchun vy shaklini ishlatadi: **Vitajte**. Vitaj — bitta doʻst uchun.

a2-u3-navsteva.mate-krasny-dom.note.en: **dom** = a house; **krásny** = beautiful, lovely. Emma says vy to Lucia's parents and grandma; they say ty to her.
a2-u3-navsteva.mate-krasny-dom.note.t: **dom** = uy (bino); **krásny** = chiroyli, goʻzal. Emma Lusiyaning ota-onasi va buvisiga vy (siz) deydi, ular esa unga ty (sen) deyishadi.

a2-u3-navsteva.build-dakujem-za-pozvanie.en: Thank you for the invitation. You have a lovely house.
a2-u3-navsteva.build-dakujem-za-pozvanie.t: Taklif uchun rahmat. Uyingiz juda chiroyli.

en: Emma says vy to Lucia's parents, so it's **máte**. Máš is for ty.
A house is **dom**. Domov is home as in where to: ísť domov.
t: Emma Lusiyaning ota-onasiga vy (siz) deydi, shuning uchun **máte**. Máš — ty uchun.

a2-u3-navsteva.sme-radi-ze-si-tu.note.en: **rád, rada, radi** + **že** = glad that. Lucia's mum on her own: Som rada, že si tu, Emma.
a2-u3-navsteva.sme-radi-ze-si-tu.note.t: **rád, rada, radi** + **že** = …ganidan xursand. Lusiyaning oyisi oʻzi gapirsa: Som rada, že si tu, Emma. = Kelganingdan xursandman, Emma.

a2-u3-navsteva.je-ti-zima.note.en: Je zima. = It's cold (out). **Je mi zima.** = I'm cold: mi and ti, to me and to you, say who feels it.
a2-u3-navsteva.je-ti-zima.note.t: Je zima. = Havo sovuq (tashqarida). **Je mi zima.** = Sovqotyapman (soʻzma-soʻz: «menga sovuq»): mi va ti (menga, senga) kim sovqotayotganini bildiradi.

a2-u3-navsteva.fill-emma-je-ti-zima.why.en: Who feels the cold is in the dative: **ti** (to you), the short form, in second place. Ťa is the object form.
a2-u3-navsteva.fill-emma-je-ti-zima.why.t: Sovuqni his qilayotgan odam datívda keladi: **ti** (senga) — qisqa shakl, ikkinchi oʻrinda. Ťa — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-navsteva.si-hladna.note.en: Thirsty is **smädný**. Babka has baked: Chceš **ochutnať** koláč? = Do you want to try a cake? (**koláč** = a cake, a pastry)
a2-u3-navsteva.si-hladna.note.t: Chanqagan — **smädný**. Buvi pirog pishirgan: Chceš **ochutnať** koláč? = Pirogdan tatib koʻrasanmi? (**koláč** = pirog)

a2-u3-navsteva.fill-si-hladna-emma.en.en: Are you hungry, Emma? Will you have some soup?

a2-u3-navsteva.fill-si-hladna-emma.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the adjective ends in **-á**: hladn**á**.
a2-u3-navsteva.fill-si-hladna-emma.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun sifat **-á** bilan tugaydi: hladn**á**.

a2-u3-navsteva.choice-emma-is-cold.quest.en: Emma is cold. What does she say?

a2-u3-navsteva.choice-emma-is-cold.why.en: **Je mi zima** says that you feel cold: mi = to me. Je zima only says it's cold out, and mám zima isn't Slovak.
a2-u3-navsteva.choice-emma-is-cold.why.t: **Je mi zima** oʻzingiz sovqotayotganingizni aytadi: mi = menga. Je zima faqat havo sovuq ekanini aytadi, mám zima esa slovakcha emas.

a2-u3-navsteva.chce-sa-mi-spat.note.en: Literally “it wants itself to me to sleep”. The same pattern: Chce sa mi jesť. = I feel like eating.
a2-u3-navsteva.chce-sa-mi-spat.note.t: Soʻzma-soʻz: «menga uxlash xohlanyapti», oʻzbekchadagi «uxlagim kelyapti»ga oʻxshaydi. Shu qolipda: Chce sa mi jesť. = Ovqat yegim kelyapti.

en: We are glad you are here, Emma.

a2-u3-navsteva.fill-chce-sa-mi-spat.why.en: Who feels like it is in the dative, so it's chce sa **mi**. Ma is the object form, ja the subject.
a2-u3-navsteva.fill-chce-sa-mi-spat.why.t: Xohishni his qilayotgan odam datívda keladi, shuning uchun chce sa **mi**. Ma — toʻldiruvchi shakli, ja — ega.

a2-u3-navsteva.build-chces-ochutnat-kola.en: Do you want to try a cake?

en: After chceš comes the infinitive, the -ť form: chceš **ochutnať**.
Koláč is a thing, so as the object it doesn't change: ochutnať **koláč**.
t: chceš dan keyin infinitív, yaʼni -ť shakli keladi: chceš **ochutnať**.
Koláč — jonsiz narsa, shuning uchun toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi: ochutnať **koláč**.

a2-u3-mi-mne.grammar-dative-pronouns.tit.en: To me, to him: mi, mu, jej

en: Pronouns have a dative too. You know **mi**, **ti** and **vám**: Páči sa mi. Zavolám ti. Ako sa vám páčila konferencia?
The short forms are small words that go in second place, like sa: Kúpim **mu** knihu. Dám **jej** šál.
t: Olmoshlarning ham datívi bor. **mi**, **ti** va **vám** ni bilasiz: Páči sa mi. Zavolám ti. Ako sa vám páčila konferencia? Bular oʻzbekchadagi menga, senga, sizga.

Qisqa shakllar sa kabi kichik soʻzlar, ular ikkinchi oʻrinda turadi: Kúpim **mu** knihu. = Unga kitob olaman. Dám **jej** šál. = Unga sharf beraman. Oʻzbekchada «unga» bitta, slovakchada esa erkakka **mu**, ayolga **jej**.

en: Use the long forms **mne, tebe, jemu** at the start of a sentence, alone as an answer, or to stress who: **Mne** sa páči, ale **jemu** nie. Komu? – **Tebe**.
A short form never starts a sentence: Páči sa **mi**, but **Mne** sa páči.
t: Uzun shakllar **mne, tebe, jemu** gap boshida, yolgʻiz javob sifatida yoki kimligini taʼkidlash uchun ishlatiladi: **Mne** sa páči, ale **jemu** nie. = Menga yoqadi, unga esa yoʻq. Komu? – **Tebe**. = Kimga? — Senga.
Qisqa shakl hech qachon gapni boshlamaydi: Páči sa **mi**, lekin **Mne** sa páči.

en: I like your scarf, but he doesn't.
Who are you giving that present to? – You.
t: Sharfing menga yoqadi, unga (erkakka) esa yoʻq.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-kupim-mu-roman.en.en: Uncle Pavol likes reading. I'll buy him a novel.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-kupim-mu-roman.en.t: Pavol togʻa kitob oʻqishni yaxshi koʻradi. Unga roman olaman.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-kupim-mu-roman.why.en: Ujo Pavol is on, so to him is **mu**. Jej is to her, im to them.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-kupim-mu-roman.why.t: Pavol togʻa — on, shuning uchun «unga» — **mu**. Jej — ayolga, im — ularga.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-komu-das-tebe.en.en: Who will you give that present to? – You.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-komu-das-tebe.why.en: Alone, as an answer, the pronoun takes its long form: **Tebe**. Ti is the short form, teba the object form.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-komu-das-tebe.why.t: Yolgʻiz, javob sifatida olmosh uzun shaklda keladi: **Tebe**. Ti — qisqa shakl, teba — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: She's the one who gets the scarf, so it's the dative: **jej**. Ju is the object form.
Mu is to him; to her is **jej**.
t: Sharfni u (ayol) oladi, shuning uchun datív: **jej**. Ju — toʻldiruvchi shakli (uni).

a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-mne-sa-paci.why.en: A short form never starts a sentence, and neither does sa. At the start, use the long form: **Mne** sa páči… (or: Páči sa mi…).
a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-mne-sa-paci.why.t: Qisqa shakl ham, sa ham gapni boshlamaydi. Gap boshida uzun shakl keladi: **Mne** sa páči… (yoki: Páči sa mi…).

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-dame-im-polievku.en.en: Lucia and Marek are hungry. We'll give them some soup.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-dame-im-polievku.en.t: Lusiya va Marekning qorni och. Ularga shoʻrva beramiz.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-dame-im-polievku.why.en: They get the soup, so it's the dative of oni: **im**. Ich is the object form or “their”.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-dame-im-polievku.why.t: Shoʻrvani ular oladi, shuning uchun oni ning datívi: **im** (ularga). Ich — toʻldiruvchi shakli (ularni) yoki «ularning».

a2-u3-mi-mne.grammar-je-mi-zima.title.en: Je mi zima: how you feel

en: Slovak often says how you feel with the dative: **Je mi zima.** = I'm cold. **Je mi ľúto.** = I'm sorry. **Chce sa mi spať.** = I'm sleepy. Swap the pronoun for someone else: Je **mu** zle. = He feels sick.
**Ako sa ti darí?** = How are you getting on? Darí sa **mi** dobre. = I'm doing well.
t: Slovak tilida holat koʻpincha datív bilan aytiladi: **Je mi zima.** = Sovqotyapman. **Je mi ľúto.** = Afsusdaman. **Chce sa mi spať.** = Uyqum kelyapti. Olmoshni almashtirsangiz, gap boshqa odam haqida boʻladi: Je **mu** zle. = Uning (erkakning) mazasi yoʻq.
**Ako sa ti darí?** = Ishlaring qalay? Darí sa **mi** dobre. = Ishlarim yaxshi.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-babka-chce-sa-jej.why.en: Who feels like sleeping is in the dative. Babka is ona, so **jej**. Ju is the object form.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-babka-chce-sa-jej.why.t: Uxlagisi kelayotgan odam datívda keladi. Babka — ona, shuning uchun **jej**. Ju — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-mi-mne.build-ako-sa-vam-dari.promp.en: How are you getting on? (Emma to babka)

en: Dariť sa takes the dative: **vám**. Vás is the object form.
Emma says vy to babka, so it's **vám**. Ti is for a friend.
t: Dariť sa datívni talab qiladi: **vám**. Vás — toʻldiruvchi shakli.
Emma buviga vy (siz) deydi, shuning uchun **vám**. Ti — doʻstga.

a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-samko-je-ti-zle.why.en: How you feel takes the dative, with the short form in second place: je **ti** zle.
a2-u3-mi-mne.fill-samko-je-ti-zle.why.t: Holat datív bilan aytiladi, qisqa shakl ikkinchi oʻrinda: je **ti** zle.

en: He doesn't like it, but I do.
t: Unga bu yoqmaydi, lekin menga yoqadi.
Unga bu yoqmaydi, menga esa yoqadi.
Bu unga yoqmaydi, lekin menga yoqadi.

a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-je-mi-to-luto.questi.en: Tomáš can't come. How does Emma say she's sorry?
a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-je-mi-to-luto.questi.t: Tomash kela olmaydi. Emma afsuslanayotganini qanday aytadi?

a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-je-mi-to-luto.why.en: The one who is sorry is in the dative: je **mi** to ľúto. Ma is the object form.
a2-u3-mi-mne.choice-je-mi-to-luto.why.t: Afsuslanayotgan odam datívda keladi: je **mi** to ľúto. Ma — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.titleEn.en: To my mum, to our uncle

a2-u3-mojej-mame.grammar-possessives-dat.en: My, your, our in the dative

en: Môj, tvoj, náš and váš change too. For him or it: **-mu** (môj**mu**, náš**mu**). For her: **-ej** (moj**ej**, naš**ej**). For more than one: **-im** (moj**im**, naš**im**). Like môjho and nášho, môjmu and nášmu keep their ô and á; mojej, našej and mojim don't.
**Jeho, jej** and **ich** never change: Dám to **jeho** mame.
t: Môj, tvoj, náš va váš ham oʻzgaradi. Erkak va oʻrta jins uchun: **-mu** (môj**mu**, náš**mu**). Ayol jinsi uchun: **-ej** (moj**ej**, naš**ej**). Koʻplik uchun: **-im** (moj**im**, naš**im**). môjho va nášho kabi, môjmu va nášmu ham ô va á ni saqlaydi; mojej, našej va mojim esa saqlamaydi.
**Jeho, jej** va **ich** hech qachon oʻzgarmaydi: Dám to **jeho** mame. = Buni uning (erkakning) onasiga beraman.

en: Will you give it to my mum?
What shall we buy your son?
You know svoj from unit 2. In the dative it goes like môj: **svojmu**, **svojej**, **svojim**.
Emma kúpi šál **svojej** mame: her own mum. **Jej** mame would be another woman's mum, say Lucia's.
t: svoj (oʻz) ni 2-boʻlimdan bilasiz. Datívda u môj kabi oʻzgaradi: **svojmu**, **svojej**, **svojim**.
Emma kúpi šál **svojej** mame: oʻz onasiga. **Jej** mame esa boshqa ayolning, masalan, Lusiyaning onasiga degani boʻlardi.

en: Emma will buy her mum a scarf.
I'll buy it for my brother.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-das-to-mojej-mame..en: Will you give it to my mum?
Mame is feminine and in the dative, so môj takes **-ej**: moj**ej** mame. Moju is the object form.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-das-to-mojej-mame..t: Mame ayol jinsida va datívda, shuning uchun môj **-ej** oladi: moj**ej** mame. Moju — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-co-kupime-tvojmu.e.en: What shall we buy your brother?

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-co-kupime-tvojmu.w.en: Bratovi is masculine dative, so tvoj takes **-mu**: tvoj**mu** bratovi. Tvojho is the object form.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-co-kupime-tvojmu.w.t: Bratovi erkak jinsida, datívda, shuning uchun tvoj **-mu** oladi: tvoj**mu** bratovi. Tvojho — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-poslem-fotky-tvoji.en: I'll send the photos to your parents.
Rodičom is plural dative, so tvoj takes **-im**: tvoj**im** rodičom. Tvojich is the object form.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-poslem-fotky-tvoji.t: Rodičom koʻplikda, datívda, shuning uchun tvoj **-im** oladi: tvoj**im** rodičom. Tvojich — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-dakujem-vasej-rodi.en: My thanks to your family for the invitation.
Ďakovať takes the dative, and rodina is feminine: **vašej** rodine. Vašu is the object form.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-dakujem-vasej-rodi.t: Ďakovať datívni talab qiladi (oʻzbekchada ham «oilangizga rahmat»), rodina esa ayol jinsida: **vašej** rodine. Vašu — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: Babka is the one who likes them, so she's in the dative, and so is náš: **našej** babke.
Papuče is plural, so the verb is **páčia** sa.
t: Ularni buvi yoqtiradi, shuning uchun u datívda, náš ham: **našej** babke (buvimizga).
Papuče — koʻplik, shuning uchun feʼl **páčia** sa.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-emma-kupi-jej-ma.en: Emma is buying a present for Lucia's mum. Emma kúpi darček ___ mame. Which word fits?
a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-emma-kupi-jej-ma.t: Emma Lusiyaning onasiga sovgʻa olyapti. Emma kúpi darček ___ mame. Qaysi soʻz mos keladi?

a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-emma-kupi-jej-ma.en: It's Lucia's mum, so “her” is **jej**, which never changes. Svojej would mean Emma's own mum.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-emma-kupi-jej-ma.t: Bu Lusiyaning onasi, shuning uchun «uning» — **jej**, u oʻzgarmaydi. Svojej — Emmaning oʻz onasi boʻlardi.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-emma-posle-svojej-.en: Emma will send her sister a postcard.
Emma is the subject and the owner, so it's **svoj**, and sestre is feminine dative: **svojej** sestre.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.fill-emma-posle-svojej-.t: Emma — gapning egasi, singil ham uniki, shuning uchun **svoj** (oʻz), sestre esa ayol jinsida, datívda: **svojej** sestre.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-nasmu-ujovi.why.en: Ujo is masculine and in the dative, so both words take the dative ending: **nášmu** ujovi.
a2-u3-mojej-mame.choice-nasmu-ujovi.why.t: Ujo erkak jinsida va datívda, shuning uchun ikkala soʻz ham datív qoʻshimchasini oladi: **nášmu** ujovi.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.build-co-kupime-vasmu-s.en: What shall we buy your son? (to uncle and aunt)

en: Synovi is in the dative, so váš takes **-mu**: váš**mu** synovi.
Your son gets the present, so he's in the dative: syn**ovi**. Syna is the object form.
t: Synovi datívda, shuning uchun váš **-mu** oladi: váš**mu** synovi.
Sovgʻani oʻgʻlingiz oladi, shuning uchun u datívda: syn**ovi** (oʻgʻlingizga). Syna — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: I'll give it to his mum.
I'll give it to his mother.

a2-u3-mojej-mame.speak-kupim-to-svojej.e.en: I'll buy it for my mum.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.stedry-vecer.note.en: The day is **Štedrý deň**. Slovaks celebrate (**oslavovať**) with a big dinner on Christmas Eve, and open their presents after it.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.stedry-vecer.note.t: Kunning oʻzi — **Štedrý deň**. Slovaklar Rojdestvo arafasida katta kechki ovqat bilan bayram qiladi (**oslavovať**), sovgʻalarni esa undan keyin ochadi.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.vianocny-stromcek.not.en: The family **zdobí** (decorates) it just before Christmas, with **ozdoby** and **salónky**, sweets in shiny paper. Under it there's often a **betlehem**, a nativity scene.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.vianocny-stromcek.not.t: Oila uni Rojdestvodan sal oldin bezatadi (**zdobí**): oʻyinchoqlar (**ozdoby**) va yaltiroq qogʻozga oʻralgan konfetlar (**salónky**) bilan. Tagida koʻpincha **betlehem** turadi — Isoning tugʻilishini tasvirlovchi kichik sahna.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.build-na-stedry-den-z.en: We decorate the tree on 24 December.

en: “We” is my, so the verb ends in **-me**: zdobíme.
One tree: **stromček**. Stromčeky is the plural.
t: «Biz» — my, shuning uchun feʼl **-me** bilan tugaydi: zdobíme.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.oplatky-s-medom.note.en: Dinner starts with thin wafers, **oplátky** (also called oblátky), with honey, **med**.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.oplatky-s-medom.note.t: Kechki ovqat yupqa vaflilar — **oplátky** (oblátky deb ham ataladi) va asal — **med** bilan boshlanadi.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.kapustnica.note.en: The Christmas soup, made from sauerkraut, often with mushrooms (**huby**) and sausage. Every family thinks theirs is the best.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.kapustnica.note.t: Rojdestvo shoʻrvasi tuzlangan karamdan, koʻpincha qoʻziqorin (**huby**) va kolbasa bilan tayyorlanadi. Har bir oila oʻzinikini eng mazalisi deb hisoblaydi.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-na-stedry-vecer-.en: On Christmas Eve we eat sauerkraut soup.
The soup is what we eat, the object, so kapustnica changes -a to **-u**.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-na-stedry-vecer-.t: Shoʻrva — biz yeydigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun kapustnica soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.kapor.note.en: Fried carp with potato salad, **zemiakový šalát**, is the main course. Some families buy a live kapor and keep it in the bath until Christmas Eve!
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.kapor.note.t: Asosiy taom — kartoshka salati (**zemiakový šalát**) bilan qovurilgan karp. Baʼzi oilalar tirik karp sotib olib, uni Rojdestvo arafasigacha vannada saqlaydi!

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.koleda.note.en: After dinner, families sing **koledy** by the tree. Late in the evening many go to church for **polnočná omša**, Midnight Mass.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.koleda.note.t: Kechki ovqatdan keyin oilalar archa yonida **koledy** kuylaydi. Kechroq koʻpchilik cherkovga yarim tungi ibodatga boradi: **polnočná omša**.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.vesele-vianoce.note.en: Children's presents come from **Ježiško**, baby Jesus, not from Father Christmas, and children write him a **list**, a letter.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.vesele-vianoce.note.t: Bolalarga sovgʻalarni Qorbobo emas, **Ježiško** — chaqaloq Iso olib keladi, bolalar esa unga xat — **list** yozadi.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-deti-pisu-list-j.en: Children write a letter to baby Jesus.
The letter goes to Ježiško, so he's in the dative, with **-ovi**: Ježišk**ovi**.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-deti-pisu-list-j.t: Xatni Ježiško oladi, shuning uchun u datívda, **-ovi** bilan: Ježišk**ovi**.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-darceky-su-pod.e.en: The presents are under the tree.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-darceky-su-pod.w.en: **Pod** (under) takes the instrumental when it says where: pod stromček**om**.
a2-u3-stedry-vecer.fill-darceky-su-pod.w.t: **Pod** (tagida) joyni bildirganda inštrumentál talab qiladi: pod stromček**om**.

en: Before dinner we decorate the tree.
After dinner we sing carols by the tree.
After dinner we open the presents.
t: Kechki ovqatdan keyin archa yonida Rojdestvo qoʻshiqlarini kuylaymiz.

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.choice-kedy-otvaraju-.en: When do Slovak children open their presents?

a2-u3-stedry-vecer.build-ako-oslavujete-.en: How do you celebrate Christmas in Ireland?

en: In Ireland answers “where?”: v + the locative, **v Írsku**. Z Írska means from Ireland.
Christmas is what you celebrate, the object, and **Vianoce** doesn't change as an object.
t: «Irlandiyada» — «qayerda?» savoliga javob: v + lokál, **v Írsku**. Z Írska — Irlandiyadan.
Rojdestvo — nishonlanadigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, **Vianoce** esa toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi.

en: Grandma makes the best sauerkraut soup.
Grandma cooks the best sauerkraut soup.
t: Buvi eng mazali karam shoʻrva pishiradi.
Buvi eng yaxshi karam shoʻrva pishiradi.
Buvi eng mazali karam shoʻrvani pishiradi.
Eng mazali karam shoʻrvani buvi pishiradi.

a2-u3-paci-sa.grammar-three-ways-like.ti.en: Mám rád, páči sa mi, chutí mi
a2-u3-paci-sa.grammar-three-ways-like.ti.t: Mám rád, páči sa mi, chutí mi

en: You know all three from A1: **mám rád** + the object form for liking someone or something in general (Mám rada babku), **páči sa mi** for what you see or hear, **chutí mi** for food and drink.
With páči sa and chutí, the thing you like is the subject, and the person is in the dative: mi, ti, babke…
t: Uchalasini A1 dan bilasiz: **mám rád** + toʻldiruvchi shakli — kimnidir yoki nimanidir umuman yaxshi koʻrish (Mám rada babku. = Buvimni yaxshi koʻraman), **páči sa mi** — koʻrgan yoki eshitgan narsangiz yoqishi, **chutí mi** — ovqat va ichimlikning taʼmi yoqishi.
Páči sa va chutí bilan yoqqan narsa ega boʻladi, odam esa datívda keladi: mi, ti, babke… Xuddi oʻzbekchadagi «menga yoqadi», «buviga yoqadi» kabi.

en: I like the sauerkraut soup. (its taste)
As in A1, the verb agrees with the thing you like: páči sa mi stromček, **páčia** sa mi ozdoby. Chutiť does the same: chutí mi koláč, **chutia** mi koláče.
In the past it agrees too: **páčil** sa mi film, **páčila** sa mi kniha, **páčili** sa mi Vianoce.
t: A1 dagi kabi, feʼl yoqqan narsaga moslashadi: páči sa mi stromček, **páčia** sa mi ozdoby. Chutiť ham shunday: chutí mi koláč, **chutia** mi koláče.
Oʻtgan zamonda ham moslashadi: **páčil** sa mi film, **páčila** sa mi kniha, **páčili** sa mi Vianoce.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-paci-sa-mi-vas-stromc.en: One tree, so the verb is singular: **Páči** sa mi stromček. Páčia is for more than one thing.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-paci-sa-mi-vas-stromc.t: Bitta archa, shuning uchun feʼl birlikda: **Páči** sa mi stromček. Páčia — bir nechta narsa uchun.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-babke-sa-pacia-koledy.en: Koledy is plural, so the verb is too: **páčia** sa. It agrees with the carols, not with babka.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-babke-sa-pacia-koledy.t: Koledy — koʻplik, shuning uchun feʼl ham koʻplikda: **páčia** sa. Feʼl babka ga emas, qoʻshiqlarga moslashadi.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-chuti-ti-kapustnica.e.en: Do you like the sauerkraut soup?

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-chuti-ti-kapustnica.w.en: With chutiť, the food is the subject, so it doesn't change: **kapustnica**. Mám rád would need the object form, kapustnicu.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-chuti-ti-kapustnica.w.t: Chutiť bilan ovqat ega boʻladi, shuning uchun oʻzgarmaydi: **kapustnica**. Mám rád bilan esa toʻldiruvchi shakli kerak boʻlardi: kapustnicu.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-mam-rada-kapustnicu.w.en: After mám rád, what you like is the object, so -a becomes **-u**: kapustnic**u**.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-mam-rada-kapustnicu.w.t: mám rád dan keyin yoqtirgan narsangiz toʻldiruvchi boʻladi, shuning uchun -a **-u** ga aylanadi: kapustnic**u**.

a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-emma-sees-scarf.que.en: Emma sees Lucia's new scarf for the first time. What does she say?
a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-emma-sees-scarf.que.t: Emma Lusiyaning yangi sharfini birinchi marta koʻryapti. U nima deydi?

a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-emma-sees-scarf.why.en: For something you see and like, say **páči sa mi**. Chutí is only for food, and mám rada is liking in general, often for a long time.
a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-emma-sees-scarf.why.t: Koʻrib yoqqan narsa uchun **páči sa mi** deyiladi. Chutí faqat ovqat uchun, mám rada esa umuman, koʻpincha uzoq vaqtdan beri yaxshi koʻrishni bildiradi.

en: Koledy is plural, so the verb is **páčia** sa.
With páčiť sa, the one who likes it is in the dative: **babke**.
t: Koledy — koʻplik, shuning uchun feʼl **páčia** sa.
páčiť sa bilan yoqtiruvchi odam datívda keladi (oʻzbekchada ham «buviga»): **babke**.

en: The past agrees with the soup: polievka is feminine, so **chutila**.
The one who likes it is in the dative: **mi**. Ma is the object form.
t: Oʻtgan zamon shoʻrvaga moslashadi: polievka ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **chutila**.
Yoqtiruvchi odam datívda keladi: **mi** (menga). Ma — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-ako-sa-vam-pacili.en.en: How did you like Christmas in Slovakia?

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-ako-sa-vam-pacili.why.en: Vianoce is plural, so the past ends in **-li**: páčili.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-ako-sa-vam-pacili.why.t: Vianoce — koʻplik, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-li** bilan tugaydi: páčili.

en: Marek is cooking Grandma's sauerkraut soup.

a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-marekovi-chuti.why.en: **Marekovi** is the dative, the one who likes it. Kapustnica is the subject, and babkina says whose it is.
a2-u3-paci-sa.choice-marekovi-chuti.why.t: **Marekovi** — datív, yaʼni yoqtiruvchi odam (Marekka). Kapustnica — ega, babkina esa kimniki ekanini aytadi.

a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-chutia-vam-kolace.why.en: Koláče is plural, so the verb is plural too: **chutia**.
a2-u3-paci-sa.fill-chutia-vam-kolace.why.t: Koláče — koʻplik, shuning uchun feʼl ham koʻplikda: **chutia**.

a2-u3-slovesa.titleEn.en: Thanks for the present: verbs with the dative
a2-u3-slovesa.titleEn.t: Sovgʻa uchun rahmat: datív bilan keladigan feʼllar

en: Many verbs have two objects: the thing, in the accusative, and the person who gets it, in the dative: dať **mame** darček, ukázať **babke** fotky, povedať **Lucii** niečo.
Some take only the dative: **pomáhať** (to help), **telefonovať** (to phone), **rozumieť** (to understand), **patriť** (to belong to).
t: Koʻp feʼllarning ikki toʻldiruvchisi bor: narsa — akuzatívda (tushum kelishigi), uni oladigan odam esa datívda: dať **mame** darček, ukázať **babke** fotky, povedať **Lucii** niečo. Oʻzbekchada ham xuddi shunday: kimga — -ga, nimani — -ni (oyimga sovgʻani bermoq).
Baʼzilari faqat datív bilan keladi: **pomáhať** (yordam bermoq), **telefonovať** (telefon qilmoq), **rozumieť** (tushunmoq), **patriť** (tegishli boʻlmoq).

en: Lucia is helping Mum in the kitchen.
**Ďakovať** takes the person in the dative and **za** + the object form for the reason: Ďakujem **ti** za darček. Ďakujeme **babke** za večeru.
With **kúpiť**, **uvariť** (to cook) and **pripraviť** (to make), you can say who it's for in two ways: Uvarím **ti** čaj. = Uvarím čaj **pre teba**.
t: **Ďakovať** odamni datívda, sababni esa **za** + toʻldiruvchi shakli bilan oladi: Ďakujem **ti** za darček. = Sovgʻa uchun senga rahmat. Ďakujeme **babke** za večeru.

**kúpiť**, **uvariť** (pishirmoq, damlamoq) va **pripraviť** (tayyorlamoq) bilan kim uchun ekanini ikki xil aytish mumkin: Uvarím **ti** čaj. = Uvarím čaj **pre teba**. (Senga choy damlayman. = Sen uchun choy damlayman.)

en: We thank Grandma for the dinner.
t: Kechki ovqat uchun buviga rahmat aytamiz.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-dakujem-ti-za-darcek..en: You thank someone **za** (for) something: ďakujem ti **za** darček.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-dakujem-ti-za-darcek..t: Kimgadir biror narsa **za** (uchun) rahmat aytiladi: ďakujem ti **za** darček.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-lucia-pomaha-mame.en.en: Lucia is helping Mum in the kitchen.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-lucia-pomaha-mame.why.en: **Pomáhať** takes the dative, so mama changes to **mame**. Mamu is the object form.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-lucia-pomaha-mame.why.t: **Pomáhať** datívni talab qiladi (oʻzbekchada ham «oyisiga yordam beradi»), shuning uchun mama **mame** ga aylanadi. Mamu — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: Grandma is the one you show them to, so she's in the dative: **babke**. Babku is the object form.
“I” is ja, so the verb ends in **-m**: ukážem.
t: Suratlarni buviga koʻrsatasiz, shuning uchun u datívda: **babke**. Babku — toʻldiruvchi shakli.
«Men» — ja, shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi: ukážem.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-na-vianoce-darujem-ma.en: For Christmas I'm giving Mum a book.
**Darovať** (to give as a present) takes the person in the dative: mam**e**. Mamu is the object form.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-na-vianoce-darujem-ma.t: **Darovať** (sovgʻa qilmoq) odamni datívda oladi: mam**e**. Mamu — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

a2-u3-slovesa.build-prepacte-nerozumiem-.en: Sorry, I don't understand you. (Emma to babka)

en: **Rozumieť** takes the dative: **vám**. Vás is the object form.
Not understanding is ne- + the verb, written as one word: **nerozumiem**.
t: **Rozumieť** datívni talab qiladi: **vám**. Oʻzbekchada «sizni tushunaman», slovakchada esa «sizga». Vás — toʻldiruvchi shakli.
Tushunmaslik — ne- + feʼl, bitta soʻz qilib yoziladi: **nerozumiem**.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-komu-patri-ten-sal.wh.en: **Patriť** (to belong) takes the dative, and Lucia becomes **Lucii**.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-komu-patri-ten-sal.wh.t: **Patriť** (tegishli boʻlmoq) datívni talab qiladi, Lucia esa **Lucii** boʻladi.

en: Like páčiť sa and chutiť, **chýbať** turns the sentence round: the one you miss is the subject, and you're in the dative.
**Chýbaš mi.** = I miss you (you are missing to me). **Chýba mi rodina.** = I miss my family. **Chýbajú mi** rodičia. = I miss my parents.
t: páčiť sa va chutiť kabi, **chýbať** ham gapni teskari qiladi: sogʻingan odamingiz ega boʻladi, siz esa datívda.
**Chýbaš mi.** = Seni sogʻindim (soʻzma-soʻz: sen menga yetishmayapsan). **Chýba mi rodina.** = Oilamni sogʻindim. **Chýbajú mi** rodičia. = Ota-onamni sogʻindim.

a2-u3-slovesa.choice-chybas-mi.question.en: Emma phones her mum in Dublin on Christmas Day. How does she say “I miss you”?
a2-u3-slovesa.choice-chybas-mi.question.t: Rojdestvo kuni Emma Dublindagi oyisiga qoʻngʻiroq qiladi. U «Seni sogʻindim»ni qanday aytadi?

a2-u3-slovesa.choice-chybas-mi.why.en: The one you miss is the subject, **chýbaš** (you are missing), and you're in the dative, **mi**. Chýbam ti would mean “you miss me”.
a2-u3-slovesa.choice-chybas-mi.why.t: Sogʻingan odamingiz — ega, **chýbaš** (sen yetishmayapsan), siz esa datívda: **mi**. Chýbam ti esa «sen meni sogʻinding» degani boʻlardi.

en: The one who misses is in the dative: **mi**. Ma is the object form.
The family is the subject, so the verb is **chýba** (it is missing). Chýbam would mean “I am missing”.
t: Sogʻinayotgan odam datívda keladi: **mi** (menga). Ma — toʻldiruvchi shakli.
Oila — ega, shuning uchun feʼl **chýba** (yetishmayapti). Chýbam «men yetishmayapman» degani boʻlardi.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-samko-slubil-babke.en.en: Samko promised Grandma he'd be good.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-samko-slubil-babke.en.t: Samko buviga odobli boʻlishini vaʼda qildi.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-samko-slubil-babke.wh.en: You promise something **to** someone, so it's the dative: babk**e**.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-samko-slubil-babke.wh.t: Biror narsani kimgadir vaʼda qilasiz, shuning uchun datív: babk**e** (buviga).

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-uvarim-caj-pre-teba.e.en: I'll make some tea for you.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-uvarim-caj-pre-teba.w.en: **Pre** takes the object form, the long one after a preposition: pre **teba**. Without pre: Uvarím **ti** čaj.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-uvarim-caj-pre-teba.w.t: **Pre** toʻldiruvchi shaklini talab qiladi, predlogdan keyin esa uzun shakl keladi: pre **teba**. pre boʻlmasa: Uvarím **ti** čaj. = Senga choy damlayman.

a2-u3-slovesa.fill-blahozelam-ti-samko.w.en: **Blahoželať** (to congratulate) takes the dative: **ti**, the short form. Ťa and teba are object forms.
a2-u3-slovesa.fill-blahozelam-ti-samko.w.t: **Blahoželať** (tabriklamoq) datívni talab qiladi: **ti**, qisqa shakl. Oʻzbekchada «seni tabriklayman», slovakchada esa «senga». Ťa va teba — toʻldiruvchi shakllari.

a2-u3-slovesa.build-dakujeme-babke-za-ve.en: We thank Grandma for the dinner.
a2-u3-slovesa.build-dakujeme-babke-za-ve.t: Kechki ovqat uchun buviga rahmat aytamiz.

en: Ďakovať takes the person in the dative: **babke**.
After **za** comes the object form: za večer**u**.
t: **za** dan keyin toʻldiruvchi shakli keladi: za večer**u**.

en: That scarf belongs to Emma, not Lucia.
That scarf belongs to Emma, not to Lucia.
t: Bu sharf Emmaga tegishli, Lusiyaga emas.

a2-u3-pocity.stastny-a-nestastny.note.en: Emma is **šťastná**: there was a present for her under the Šimkos' tree too.
a2-u3-pocity.stastny-a-nestastny.note.t: Emma **šťastná**: Shimkolarning archasi tagida unga ham sovgʻa bor edi.

a2-u3-pocity.fill-emma-je-stastna.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the adjective ends in **-á**: šťastn**á**.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-emma-je-stastna.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun sifat **-á** bilan tugaydi: šťastn**á**.

a2-u3-pocity.prekvapeny.note.en: You met prekvapený in unit 2: pán Kováč wasn't angry, just surprised. A surprise is a **prekvapenie**: To je prekvapenie!
a2-u3-pocity.prekvapeny.note.t: prekvapený ni 2-boʻlimda uchratgansiz: janob Kovachning jahli chiqmagan, u shunchaki hayron boʻlgan edi. Syurpriz — **prekvapenie**: To je prekvapenie!

en: Samko is a boy, so it's nahnevan**ý**.
You're asking Samko himself (ty), so byť is **si**.
t: Samko — oʻgʻil bola, shuning uchun nahnevan**ý**.
Siz Samkoning oʻzidan soʻrayapsiz (ty), shuning uchun byť — **si**.

a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-je-nahnevany-pre.en: Samko is cross because he has to go to bed.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-je-nahnevany-pre.t: Samkoning jahli chiqqan, chunki u uxlashga yotishi kerak.

a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-je-nahnevany-pre.en: **Pretože** (because) gives the reason. Prečo asks why.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-je-nahnevany-pre.t: **Pretože** (chunki) sababni aytadi. Prečo esa «nega?» deb soʻraydi.

a2-u3-pocity.zalubeny.note.en: Ujo Pavol a teta Mirka sú stále **zaľúbení**. (**stále** = still, all the time)
a2-u3-pocity.zalubeny.note.t: Ujo Pavol a teta Mirka sú stále **zaľúbení**. = Pavol togʻa va Mirka yanga hali ham bir-biriga oshiq. (**stále** = hali ham, doim)

a2-u3-pocity.fill-ujo-a-teta-su-zalubeni.en: Uncle Pavol and Aunt Mirka are still in love.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-ujo-a-teta-su-zalubeni.t: Pavol togʻa va Mirka yanga hali ham bir-biriga oshiq.

a2-u3-pocity.fill-ujo-a-teta-su-zalubeni.en: A man and a woman together count as men, so the adjective ends in **-í**: zaľúben**í**.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-ujo-a-teta-su-zalubeni.t: Erkak va ayol birga erkaklar kabi hisoblanadi, shuning uchun sifat **-í** bilan tugaydi: zaľúben**í**.

a2-u3-pocity.bojim-sa.note.en: **báť sa** = to be afraid: bojím sa, bojíš sa, bojí sa… Nebojím sa! = I'm not scared!
a2-u3-pocity.bojim-sa.note.t: **báť sa** = qoʻrqmoq: bojím sa, bojíš sa, bojí sa… Nebojím sa! = Qoʻrqmayman!

a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-sa-boji.en.en: Samko is afraid that baby Jesus won't come.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-sa-boji.en.t: Samko chaqaloq Iso kelmay qolishidan qoʻrqyapti.

a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-sa-boji.why.en: Samko is on, so the verb has no ending: **bojí** sa. Bojím goes with ja, boja with oni.
a2-u3-pocity.fill-samko-sa-boji.why.t: Samko — on, shuning uchun feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: **bojí** sa. Bojím — ja bilan, boja — oni bilan.

a2-u3-pocity.build-dnes-je-samko-stastne.en: Today Samko is happier than yesterday.

en: Samko is a boy, so the comparative ends in **-í**: šťastnejš**í**.
Comparing with yesterday takes the comparative, **šťastnejší** ako… Naj- is for the happiest of all.
t: Samko — oʻgʻil bola, shuning uchun qiyosiy daraja **-í** bilan tugaydi: šťastnejš**í**.
Kecha bilan taqqoslash — qiyosiy daraja: **šťastnejší** ako… Naj- esa hammasidan baxtli (eng baxtli) uchun.

en: Emma is a bit tired; she's going home.
Emma is a bit sad; she misses her family.
Emma is happy; her family is coming.

**k** + the dative means towards someone or something, or to someone's place: Ideme **k** ujovi. = We're going to uncle's. Sadneme si **k** stolu. = We'll sit down at the table. It also gives the occasion: darček **k** Vianociam.
Before a word starting with k or g, and before mne, it's **ku**: **ku** kamarátovi, **ku** mne. After k, on, ona and oni start with n-: k **nemu**, k **nej**, k **nim**.
Things take **-u**, not -ovi: stôl → k stol**u**, okno → k okn**u**. -ovi is for people and animals.
t: **k** + datív — kimgadir yoki nimagadir tomon, yoki kimningdir uyiga, oʻzbekchadagi -ga, -nikiga kabi: Ideme **k** ujovi. = Togʻamnikiga boramiz. Sadneme si **k** stolu. = Stolga oʻtiramiz. Munosabatni ham bildiradi: darček **k** Vianociam (Rojdestvoga sovgʻa).
k yoki g bilan boshlanadigan soʻzdan oldin va mne dan oldin **ku** boʻladi: **ku** kamarátovi, **ku** mne. k dan keyin on, ona va oni n- bilan boshlanadi: k **nemu**, k **nej**, k **nim**.
Narsalar -ovi emas, **-u** oladi: stôl → k stol**u**, okno → k okn**u**. -ovi odamlar va hayvonlar uchun.

en: We're going to Grandma's for Christmas.
Will you come to my place?
Six more prepositions take the dative. New words here: **chrípka** (flu) and **von** (out). You know sneh (snow) and stanica (station).
**Vďaka** is for a good cause, **kvôli** for a bad or neutral one: Vďaka babke je večera výborná. Kvôli snehu mešká vlak.
t: Yana oltita predlog datív bilan keladi. Yangi soʻzlar: **chrípka** (gripp) va **von** (tashqariga). sneh (qor) va stanica (vokzal) ni bilasiz.
**Vďaka** yaxshi sabab uchun ishlatiladi, oʻzbekchadagi «sharofati bilan» kabi, **kvôli** esa yomon yoki betaraf sabab uchun, «tufayli» kabi: Vďaka babke je večera výborná. Kvôli snehu mešká vlak.
